guide_enrichment.narrative:
For us, the case for James Madison starts with the expected imbalance in scoring opportunities. Our numbers rate James Madison among the nation’s best at creating those chances, while Georgia State has struggled to prevent them. On the other side, we see Georgia State facing a defense that has been difficult to move the ball against consistently. Through four games, James Madison allowed 12.3 points and 293.3 total yards per game, and opponents converted only 35.3% of their third downs.

We also see enough offensive balance to support separation rather than merely control. James Madison averaged 199.3 rushing yards and 44.8 points through four games, while scoring on 91.7% of its red-zone possessions. Those early results do not guarantee the same efficiency here, but they align with our longer-run matchup numbers, particularly against a Georgia State defense our model views as vulnerable to the run.

Our main concern is the limited sample behind a heavily rebuilt roster. James Madison entered the season with 61 newcomers and only five returning starters, so we should not treat four games as definitive. Still, the performance to date supports the areas our model already favors, which is why we think the market is leaving James Madison with room to create separation.
guide_enrichment.matchup_to_watch:
We are watching James Madison’s rushing offense against Georgia State’s run defense. Our metrics place those units far apart, and James Madison has already shown it can distribute the workload: George Pettaway had 291 rushing yards and four touchdowns through four games, while Nick Herman added 214 yards and two scores.

That matters because productive early-down rushing can keep James Madison ahead of schedule and create repeated scoring opportunities. For us, this matchup is the clearest path to sustained drives and the margin our position requires.

recent_game.fact: James Madison improved to 4-0 with a 46-20 win at Old Dominion on Sept. 26, 2026.
JMU tied its FBS program record with nine sacks and held Old Dominion to minus-14 rushing yards.
Camden Coleman completed 24 of 42 passes for 243 yards and four touchdowns against Old Dominion, with each touchdown going to a different receiver.
George Pettaway rushed 16 times for 110 yards against Old Dominion, his third career 100-yard rushing game.
Linebacker Nakian Jackson led JMU with nine tackles for the second consecutive game and added 2.0 tackles for loss and 1.5 sacks at Old Dominion.

opponent_notes.fact: Georgia State was 3-1 overall and had not yet played a Sun Belt game through Sept. 26, 2026.
Georgia State defeated Northern Illinois 35-14 on Sept. 26, 2026.

quarterback.fact: Camden Coleman had started three of JMU's first four games and completed 59 of 95 passes for 716 yards, seven touchdowns and one interception; he also had 49 rushing yards and one rushing touchdown.
Coleman was named Sun Belt Offensive Player of the Week after throwing four touchdown passes at Old Dominion.
JC Evans started the opener against Liberty and completed 7 of 9 passes for 61 yards and a touchdown while rushing nine times for 69 yards.
Arrington Maiden completed 7 of 8 passes for 111 yards and two touchdowns in his JMU debut against Wagner.

offensive_personnel.fact: JMU returned only one offensive starter from 2025: center Zach Greenberg.
Through four games, George Pettaway had 60 carries for 291 yards and four touchdowns, while Nick Herman had 29 carries for 214 yards and two touchdowns.
Corey Scott led JMU with 16 receptions and had 185 receiving yards and two touchdowns through four games.
Braeden Wisloski had 13 receptions for 165 yards through four games, including five catches for 90 yards at San Diego State.
Tight end Cole Keller had nine receptions for 128 yards and three touchdowns through four starts.

Offensive linemen Tyler Brown, Deacon Rawls, Evan Bushong and DJ Fox each started JMU's first four games; Zach Greenberg had three starts and Noel Portnjagin made his first collegiate start at Old Dominion.

defensive_personnel.fact: JMU returned two defensive starters from 2025: edge Amar Thomas and linebacker Gannon Weathersby.
Transfer linebacker Nakian Jackson led JMU with 34 tackles through four starts and had 2.5 tackles for loss and 1.5 sacks.
Transfer linebacker JT Hooten had 19 tackles, 4.5 tackles for loss, 2.5 sacks and an interception through four starts.
Cornerback Ken Willis had 22 tackles, 4.0 tackles for loss, four pass breakups, one sack, one forced fumble and one fumble recovery through four starts.
Kevin Roberts and Kei'Trone Simpson each recorded 1.5 sacks in the win at Old Dominion.
Safety Seth Gathers made his first four collegiate starts and totaled 17 tackles and one pass breakup.

coaching_changes.fact: Billy Napier was hired as JMU's head coach on Dec. 6, 2025 and was 4-0 in his first season through four games.
JMU's first-year coordinators are offensive coordinator Cam Aiken, defensive coordinator Robert Bala and special teams coordinator Rob Wenger.
Aiken and Bala coach from the booth, while Wenger works on the field.
